## Purpose

The order state machine and its guarantees: every order has exactly one lifecycle, every transition is recorded, and no transition can be skipped.

## Depends on

- [`09-risk`](09-risk.md) — Risk Engine

## Depended on by

- [`11-execution`](11-execution.md) — Execution Core
- [`13-lp-connectivity`](13-lp-connectivity.md) — LP / FIX Connectivity
- [`19-client-api`](19-client-api.md) — Client API

## Inputs

- order intents
- risk decisions
- executions

## Outputs

- Order
- order state transitions
- client order events

## What gets built

- state machine: NEW -> VALIDATING -> RISK_CHECK -> ACCEPTED -> EXECUTING -> FILLED/PARTIAL -> POSITION_UPDATED -> SETTLED
- terminal states: REJECTED, CANCELLED, EXPIRED
- client idempotency keys
- cancel/replace with race resolution
- timeout, retry and reconciliation of unknown-state orders

## Invariants

These are executed as tests at gate **G4**. A module may not declare an
invariant it does not test.

- INV-090: an order occupies exactly one state at a time; every transition is legal and recorded.
- INV-091: a client order id maps to at most one order, forever.
- INV-092: a cancel that races a fill resolves to exactly one outcome, never both.
- INV-093: an order in an unknown execution state is never assumed to be either filled or unfilled.

## Test obligations

- exhaustive legal/illegal transition matrix
- duplicate order submission, duplicate execution report
- cancel/fill race, timeout, disconnect, late execution report
- retry storm produces exactly one order

## Known failure modes

The things that go wrong in systems like this one. Each should map to a test above.

- timeout treated as rejection while the venue actually filled
- retry creating a second order under a new id
